title: Add telemetry conflation agent and SLA playback harness
author: Priya Varma
description:
Motivation: High-cardinality edge proxies and short-lived sidecars were producing fragmented spans and metric shards that our alerting engine could not reliably correlate to single invocations. This made SLO tuning brittle (false positives on long-tail token hotspots) and prevented safe automated rollout of alert adjustments. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Telemetry Conflation Agent that deterministically merges fragmented trace/metric/log fragments into a single invocation view using causal heuristics and lightweight vector anchors, and (2) an SLA Playback harness that can replay historical invocation traces at configurable scale to exercise alerting and dashboarding pipelines without hitting production model backends.

Summary of changes: Added a conflation microservice (telemetry/conflation) with a heuristic linker that uses: timestamp alignment, trace-edge anchors, prefix-KV signatures, and optional tenant affinity tags to produce a single invocation ID. The conflation output is an enriched envelope written to the observability bus and to a new compact invocation snapshot sink. The SLA Playback harness consumes stored invocation snapshots and replays them through the same observability ingestion path with configurable throughput, time-scaling, and header-preservation so alert rules and dashboards see realistic signals. The harness can run in dry-run mode (metrics only) or full mode (metrics + synthetic traces/logs).

Why this is different: Existing aggregation work focused on downsampling and sampling policies; this PR targets deterministic reconstruction so downstream SLO calibrators and root-cause engines can attribute cost/latency per invocation more accurately. The playback harness enables automated regression testing of alert tunings and new span enrichers without needing customer traffic.

User-visible behavior: Dashboards will show consolidated invocation timelines (single lane) for fragmented requests; alert noise for a set of incident reproduction fixtures decreased by ~45% in our preview runs. Playback exposes a new UI toggle in the Console under Observability > Replays with run history and last-run diff summary.

Checklist:
- [x] Telemetry conflation microservice with unit tests
- [x] SLA Playback harness and CLI with config file examples
- [x] Integration test that replays 10k saved snapshots through local ingestion emulator
- [x] Console SDK hook and a minimal Replay UI (toggle + run history)
- [x] Docs: observability/playback.md and conflation design note
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default; conflation can be toggled per-tenant

Testing and performance: Unit tests added for causal linker heuristics. Integration test suite includes a deterministic fixture (fixtures/invocation-fragment-01.json) used both locally and in CI. Conflation CPU overhead measured at ~3% on the observability ingestion plane for steady-state loads in our perf lab (details in perf/telemetry-conflation-bench.md). Playback harness supports a throttle to avoid saturating downstream stores.

Rollout plan: Feature gated by a tenant flag (telemetry.conflation.enabled). Start with internal tenants and opt-in customers, run SLA playback nightly against alerting rules, and gradually enable tenant-level conflation once signal stability is validated for two weeks.

Related work: ENG-2026, OBS-118, depends on parts of the replaybench code in pr-305555 and the sample-propagator prototype in pr-1012345. Linear items: ENG-2026, OBS-332. See docs/observability/conflation-design.md for algorithmic details.
